chunks: From him, from Yunus, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Umayyah Yusuf ibn Thabit, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A deed does not harm along with faith, and a deed does not benefit along with disbelief.'

Do you not see that He said: 'And nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and in His Messenger, and they died while they were disbelievers.'
ai.seo_question: Does faith protect a believer from the negative effects of their sins?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the primacy of faith (Iman) as the foundational state that preserves the validity of good deeds despite accompanying sins, while total disbelief (Kufr) nullifies all acts of worship. He substantiates this principle by citing Surah At-Tawbah 9:54, highlighting that the rejection of the disbelievers' charity was due to their core rejection of Allah and His Messenger, illustrating that ritual acts without sincere belief are spiritually void.

en.hubeali: From him, from Yunus, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Abu Ameyt Yusuf Bin Sabit who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Along with Emān, no deed would harm you, nor would a deed benefit you along with Kufr (disbelief).

Do you not see that Heazwj Said [9:54] And nothing hinders their spending being Accepted from them, except that they disbelieve in Allah and in His Rasool, and they are dying while they are disbelievers (Kafiroun)’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Yunus from ibn Bukayr from abu ‘Umayyah Yusuf ibn Thabit who has said the following:
“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘With belief no deed can harm one and with disbelief no deed can benefit one.

Consider how Allah has said it, ‘What prevents their offerings from acceptance is their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger, their lack of interest in prayer and spending for the cause of Allah reluctantly, [9:54] ‘. . . and they die as disbelievers.’” [9:125]
